enhanced.fullText:
The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Grants Policy Statement, codified under 45 CFR Part 75 and supplemented by agency-specific guidance, establishes comprehensive terms and conditions governing discretionary grant and cooperative agreement awards to organizational entities. This policy framework, derived from statutory authority under 31 U.S.C. § 6301-6308 (Federal Grant and Cooperative Agreement Act) and 42 U.S.C. § 216 (Public Health Service Act), applies exclusively to HHS discretionary grant programs administered by Operating Divisions excluding the National Institutes of Health.

Higher education institutions receiving HHS discretionary awards must comply with uniform administrative requirements outlined in 2 CFR Part 200 (Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards). Key provisions include pre-award requirements mandating institutional capability demonstrations, detailed budget justifications, and compliance certifications regarding debarment, drug-free workplace policies per 2 CFR Part 180, and lobbying restrictions under 31 U.S.C. § 1352.

Post-award obligations encompass financial management systems meeting federal standards under 2 CFR § 200.302, procurement procedures adhering to competitive standards per 2 CFR §§ 200.317-200.326, and property management protocols specified in 2 CFR §§ 200.310-200.316. Universities must maintain accounting records supporting grant expenditures for three years following final expenditure reports per 2 CFR § 200.333.

The policy mandates institutional compliance with cross-cutting federal requirements including Title VI (42 U.S.C. § 2000d), Title IX (20 U.S.C. § 1681), Section 504 (29 U.S.C. § 794), Americans with Disabilities Act (42 U.S.C. § 12101), and Age Discrimination Act (42 U.S.C. § 6101). Research-related awards require adherence to human subjects protection protocols under 45 CFR Part 46 and animal welfare standards per 9 CFR Parts 1-4.

Enforcement mechanisms include award suspension, termination, and recipient debarment procedures outlined in 2 CFR Part 180. Non-compliance may result in repayment obligations, future funding restrictions, and referral to federal enforcement agencies. Recent updates incorporated governmentwide guidance on indirect cost negotiations, executive compensation limitations per 2 CFR § 200.430, and enhanced financial conflict of interest requirements under 42 CFR Part 50, Subpart F.
enhanced.summary: HHS Grants Policy Statement establishes comprehensive terms for discretionary grants to higher education institutions under 45 CFR Part 75 and 2 CFR Part 200, requiring compliance with federal administrative, financial, and programmatic standards.
enhanced.requirements:
## Pre-Award Compliance
- Submit institutional capability certifications per 2 CFR § 200.205
- Provide detailed budget justifications meeting 2 CFR § 200.211 standards
- Execute required assurances regarding debarment, drug-free workplace, and lobbying restrictions

## Financial Management
- Establish financial management systems meeting 2 CFR § 200.302 requirements
- Implement procurement procedures adhering to 2 CFR §§ 200.317-200.326
- Maintain cost documentation supporting allowability determinations under 2 CFR Part 200, Subpart E

## Administrative Oversight
- Designate authorized organizational representatives for award administration
- Implement property management systems per 2 CFR §§ 200.310-200.316
- Ensure compliance with cross-cutting federal civil rights requirements

## Record Retention
- Maintain financial and programmatic records for three years following final expenditure report submission per 2 CFR § 200.333
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Institutions must submit Federal Financial Reports (SF-425) annually or as specified in award terms, final expenditure reports within 120 days of award expiration per 2 CFR § 200.343, and performance reports according to award-specific schedules, typically annually.
